summary: James Darmesteter (1849–1894) was an Iranian, Central Asian, linguistics, and Indology scholar. He studied at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1872–1877) under Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault and Michel Bréal, later holding posts there (~1877–1894) and at the Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1964) and under Sheldon Pollock. In 1971, he became Professor Emeritus at the University of Iowa.
James Dwight Dana (1813–1895) studied at Yale College (~1830–1833). He later held a post at Yale University from circa 1850 to 1892.
James Fergusson (1808–1886) worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School and became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1840.

James Fieser (born 1958) works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Berea College (~1976–1980) and Purdue University (~1981–1986). Around 1992, he held posts at the University of Tennessee and the University of Tennessee at Martin.

James G. Mullens is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned degrees from Simon Fraser University, the University of Victoria, and McMaster University (PhD, 1994), studying under Graeme MacQueen, Yün-hua Jan, and John G. Arapura. He held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James H. Austin (born 1925) is a Buddhist studies scholar and neurologist. He studied under Nanrei Sohaku Kobori and Katsujo Terayama, and held positions at Oregon Health & Science University, the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, and the University of Idaho.

James Hadley (1821–1872) was a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at Fairfield Academy and Yale (under Edward Elbridge Salisbury in 1849). He served as a tutor at Middlebury College (1845) and as Professor of Greek at Yale (1845–1872).

James Haughton Woods (1864–1935) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Harvard College, the University of Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen, Charles Rockwell Lanman, Arthur Venis, and Mukunda Shastri Adkar. He served as professor at Harvard University (~1903–1934).

James Irving Manatt (1845–1915) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell College and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts at Denison College, Marietta College, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and served as professor at Brown University (~1892–1915).

James Ishmael Ford (born 1948) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Sonoma State University, Pacific School of Religion, and under Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant. He founded the Boundless Way Zen and Empty Moon Zen Network.

James Kenneth Powell II is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Northwestern University, the University of Chicago, and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1998), studying under David Tracy, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald (born 1948) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago under Edwin Gerow and J. A. B. van Buitenen. He held posts at the University of Tennessee and served as Das Professor at Brown University.

James L. Taylor is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Macquarie University in 1989 and held a post as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide, attested in 2014.

James Legge (1815–1897) was a sinologist. He studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen (~1831–1835), and Highbury College (~1836–1839). In 1876, he became a professor at the University of Oxford.

James Luther Adams (1901–1994) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, later holding a post at Harvard University from circa 1956 to 1968.

James Mackintosh (1765–1832) was a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen, its School of Law, and the University of Edinburgh. He founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and served as its president (~1804–1811).

James Mallinson (born 1970) is an Indology scholar who studied at SOAS and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at SOAS and became Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford in 2023, later directing graduate studies at Wolfson College.

James Mark Shields (born 1971) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was attested as Associate Professor at Bucknell University and as an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
James Matthew Baskind is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein, attested in 2006.
